title: Microsoft Purview: lifecycle status controls for adaptive scope recipients and site owners
summary: The briefing accurately separates the planned lifecycle controls from the existing scope-query and membership tools. The supplied notice supports the active-only default and rollout targets, and Microsoft Learn supports the licensing, paths and commands shown.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans lifecycle-state evaluation controls for adaptive scope recipients and site owners.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview Adaptive Scopes will provide administrators with explicit control over lifecycle-state evaluation for recipients and site owners

claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development"

claims.claim: The roadmap lists General Availability and Preview release phases.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.claim: The roadmap record was modified on 2026-11-17T00:31:56.
An adaptive scope uses a query to define changing membership of users, groups or sites.
claims.quote: An adaptive scope uses a query that you specify, so you can define the membership of users or groups included in that query. These dynamic queries run daily against the attributes or properties that you specify for the selected scope.

claims.claim: Communication compliance, retention and auto-labeling policies can use adaptive scopes.
claims.quote: When you create a communication compliance policy, a policy for retention, or an auto-labeling policy, you can add an adaptive scope for your policy.

claims.claim: The planned controls let administrators decide whether active, inactive and soft-deleted recipients and site owners are included in scope membership.
claims.quote: This update gives administrators explicit control over whether active, inactive, and soft-deleted recipients and site owners are included in adaptive scope membership.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The change enforces active-only evaluation by default for newly created scopes, supporting defaultState on.
claims.quote: With this change, newly created adaptive scopes will evaluate only active recipients and site owners by default.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: New scopes exclude inactive recipients and site owners unless an administrator explicitly includes them.
claims.quote: Inactive and soft-deleted recipients or site owners will not be included unless explicitly configured by an administrator.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: New scopes exclude soft-deleted recipients and site owners unless an administrator explicitly includes them.
claims.quote: Inactive and soft-deleted recipients or site owners will not be included unless explicitly configured by an administrator.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Existing scopes retain their current behavior and are not automatically modified by rollout.
claims.quote: Existing adaptive scopes will continue to function as they do today and will not be automatically modified as part of this rollout.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Administrators will be able to update existing scopes to use explicit lifecycle criteria.
claims.quote: Administrators will also have the option to update existing adaptive scopes to use explicit lifecycle status evaluation criteria for recipients and site owners.

claims.quote: This update also adds support for ISO 8601 duration values for selected date attributes in the adaptive scope advanced query builder.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: The supplied notice does not name the date attributes that support durations.
claims.quote: Searched: read MC1450128 in full for date property names; it says only selected date attributes and certain date-based attributes.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn already documents relative date filters using ISO 8601 durations in the advanced query builder.
claims.quote: Use relative date filters in the advanced query builder to define scope membership by a rolling date range instead of a fixed date.

claims.claim: The Adaptive scopes page lists supported date properties under Use relative date filters.
claims.quote: Users and Microsoft 365 Groups | WhenCreated, WhenCreatedUTC, WhenMailboxCreated, WhenChanged, WhenChangedUTC, WhenSoftDeleted | SharePoint sites | Created, RefinableDate00 through RefinableDate19

claims.where: controls[0]; What's changing; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: As of November 2026, no admin UI setting or automation for the planned lifecycle membership control is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview adaptive scope lifecycle status recipients site owners soft deleted PowerShell setting licensing; adaptive scopes soft-deleted site owners setting. Opened Adaptive scopes, New-AdaptiveScope and Set-AdaptiveScope; no lifecycle setting or parameter.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; controls[1].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: Creating an adaptive scope requires a role group containing Scope Manager.
claims.quote: You need to assign the correct role groups to admins to create an adaptive scope. Any role group with the Scope Manager role can create an adaptive scope.

claims.claim: Learn lists Compliance Administrator, Compliance Data Administrator, Organization Management, Records Management, Communication Compliance and Communication Compliance Admins as built-in groups containing Scope Manager.
claims.quote: The Scope Manger role is included in the following built-in role groups: Compliance Administrator; Compliance Data Administrator; Organization Management; Records Management; Communication Compliance; Communication Compliance Admins

claims.claim: Adaptive scope queries run daily.
claims.quote: These dynamic queries run daily against the attributes or properties that you specify for the selected scope.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Queries can take up to five days to populate, and Learn advises waiting before adding a new scope to a policy.
claims.quote: It can take up to five days for the queries to fully populate and changes aren't immediate. Factor in this delay by waiting a few days before you add a newly created scope to a policy.

claims.claim: The scope query builder is reached in Microsoft Purview through Settings > Roles and scopes > Adaptive scopes > + Create scope > administrative unit > scope type > Advanced query builder.
claims.quote: Settings > Roles and scopes > Adaptive scopes. On the Adaptive scopes page, select + Create scope. Follow the prompts ... assign an administrative unit. Select the type of scope ... Alternatively, you can select Advanced query builder

claims.claim: New-AdaptiveScope -Name <name> -LocationType User -RawQuery <OPATH query> creates a user adaptive scope using the specified advanced query.
claims.quote: New-AdaptiveScope -Name <String> -LocationType <DynamicBoundaryLocationType> -RawQuery <String> ... The RawQuery parameter switches the scope to advanced query mode. You use OPATH filter syntax for advanced query mode.

claims.where: controls[2].ui; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Scope membership is reached through Microsoft Purview Settings > Roles and scopes > Adaptive scopes > scope > Details > Scope details.
claims.quote: Select Settings > Roles and scopes > Adaptive scopes. Select an existing adaptive scope from the list. From the Details flyout pane, select Scope details.

claims.claim: Get-AdaptiveScopeMembers -Identity <scope name> -State Added retrieves current scope members, and State can also select removed members.
claims.quote: Get-AdaptiveScopeMembers -Identity "US Finance Users" -State Added ... Added: Current members of the adaptive scope. Removed: Former members of the adaptive scope.

claims.claim: The membership State column identifies current members as Added.
claims.quote: Review the State column in the list that shows Added for members within the adaptive scope

claims.claim: The membership State column identifies former members that no longer match the query as Removed.
claims.quote: Removed if the member was previously in the adaptive scope but removed now they no longer match the scope query.

claims.claim: The member details list can take up to five days to reflect added or removed members.
claims.quote: It might take up to five days for the member details list to update added or removed members.

claims.claim: The included licensing model represents an option within adaptive scopes under the named existing retention licensing requirements.
claims.quote: If the retention policy uses an adaptive policy scope, then one of the following licenses is required to provide user rights:

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Retention policies using adaptive scopes require one of the five licence families listed in the briefing.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5; Microsoft Purview Suite/EDU/GOV/FLW; Microsoft Defender + Purview Suite FLW; Office 365 E5/A5/G5; Microsoft 365 E5/A5/F5/G5 Information Protection and Governance

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Any additional licence requirement specific to the lifecycle controls is not yet published as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview adaptive scopes lifecycle status controls price meter additional license. Opened Microsoft Purview service description and Adaptive scopes; read roadmap and MC1450128. Existing adaptive-scope licences are stated, but no additional lifecycle-control requirement.

claims.claim: Learn says users without a valid adaptive scopes licence do not have policy settings applied.
claims.quote: it might be because it includes users who don't have a valid license for adaptive scopes. These users don't have the policy settings applied to them.

claims.claim: The Adaptive scopes page's unlicensed-user passage does not itself name a licence.
claims.quote: Searched: read the Adaptive scopes validation tip for licence names; it says valid license for adaptive scopes without naming a plan. The briefing separately cites the service description's named licences.

claims.claim: The notice identifies Purview administrators who create or manage adaptive scopes as affected.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview administrators who create or manage adaptive scopes.

claims.claim: The notice identifies organizations using adaptive scopes for Purview policy targeting as affected.
claims.quote: Organizations that use adaptive scopes for Microsoft Purview policy targeting.

claims.claim: The notice describes no end-user change.
claims.quote: Searched: read MC1450128 in full, including Who is affected and What will happen; changes described are scope evaluation and administrator configuration, not an end-user experience.

claims.claim: Neither the roadmap record nor the notice describes a new identity or permission model.
claims.quote: Searched: read the roadmap description and MC1450128 in full for identity, permissions and role requirements; neither describes a new model.

claims.claim: A role specifically for changing the planned lifecycle setting is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: adaptive scopes lifecycle role PowerShell. Opened Adaptive scopes, New-AdaptiveScope and Set-AdaptiveScope; read MC1450128. Scope creation permissions are documented, but no lifecycle-setting-specific role.

claims.claim: The supplied descriptions do not describe an agent or autonomous action mechanism.
claims.quote: Searched: read the roadmap, MC1450128 and Adaptive scopes for agents or autonomous actions. They describe administrator controls and scheduled scope queries, not an agent.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not specifically state whether changes to the planned lifecycle settings follow the existing evaluation timing.
claims.quote: Searched: adaptive scopes lifecycle licensing default evaluation timing. Opened Adaptive scopes, New-AdaptiveScope and Set-AdaptiveScope; read MC1450128. Existing query timing is documented; lifecycle-setting propagation is not.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: The notice does not explicitly discuss the default for scripted versus portal scope creation.
claims.quote: Searched: read MC1450128 in full for PowerShell, script, API and portal distinctions. It says newly created adaptive scopes without naming a creation surface.

claims.claim: The notice does not explain how recipient and site-owner lifecycle controls map to the three adaptive scope types.
claims.quote: Searched: read MC1450128 for Users, SharePoint sites and Microsoft 365 Groups scope-type mapping. It names recipients and site owners but gives no per-type mapping; Adaptive scopes has no lifecycle configuration section.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The existing advanced query builder uses IsInactiveMailbox to exclude or specifically target inactive mailboxes.
claims.quote: You must use the advanced query builder if you want to exclude inactive mailboxes. Or conversely, target just inactive mailboxes. For this configuration, use the OPATH property IsInactiveMailbox

claims.claim: Learn documents no equivalent membership-inclusion filter for soft-deleted recipients or site owners.
claims.quote: Searched: adaptive scopes soft-deleted site owners setting. Opened Adaptive scopes and New-AdaptiveScope. Relative-date documentation says a WhenSoftDeleted filter doesn't by itself make a deleted recipient eligible for scope membership; no equivalent inclusion control found.

claims.claim: Scope creation can retain Full directory when not restricting the scope by administrative unit.
claims.quote: If you don't want to restrict the adaptive scope by using administrative units, or your organization hasn't configured administrative units, keep the default of Full directory.

claims.claim: Users is the scope-type choice for the documented user-scope query route.
claims.quote: first select Users as the scope type

claims.claim: Using New-AdaptiveScope in Security & Compliance PowerShell requires assigned Purview compliance permissions.
claims.quote: To use this cmdlet in Security & Compliance PowerShell, you need to be assigned permissions. For more information, see Permissions in the Microsoft Purview compliance portal.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends reviewing current adaptive scope configurations and governance requirements.
claims.quote: Review current adaptive scope configurations and governance requirements.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends deciding whether future scopes should include inactive or soft-deleted recipients and site owners.
claims.quote: Determine whether inactive or soft-deleted recipients and site owners should be included in future adaptive scope definitions.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends updating adaptive scope creation processes and documentation where applicable.
claims.quote: Update adaptive scope creation processes and documentation, if applicable, to account for the new lifecycle status settings.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not described specific policy outcomes from the new lifecycle membership controls beyond their targeting behavior.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview adaptive scopes lifecycle status policy outcomes inactive soft deleted retention evaluation controls. Read MC1450128 and Adaptive scopes; the notice specifies membership behavior, not downstream retention or labeling outcomes.

claims.where: front matter: cost; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The sources publish no additional direct charge for the lifecycle controls, so the low cost assessment is limited to administrative work and preserves the licensing uncertainty.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview adaptive scopes lifecycle status controls price meter additional license. Opened Microsoft Purview service description and Adaptive scopes; read MC1450128. No lifecycle-specific charge or meter found; existing licence requirements are stated separately.

claims.claim: The documented scope types are Users, SharePoint sites and Microsoft 365 Groups, and the query tools shown are existing capabilities rather than the new lifecycle switch.
claims.quote: There are three different types of adaptive scopes ... Users ... SharePoint sites ... Microsoft 365 Groups ... You must use the advanced query builder if you want to exclude inactive mailboxes.
